answer.location_description: Small patch in the top-right corner of the image, about rows 0-3 and columns 22-23 (strongest in rows 0-2).
answer.mechanism: Many first-layer units share a consistent, sharply localized weight blob in the top-right corner that is unrelated to their nodule-shaped receptive fields. The benign-leaning units (0, 2, 3, 13, 15, 18, 20, 27, 28, 31; bright-small-core detectors) carry negative corner weights. The malignant-leaning units (6, 9, 30; dark-core / bright-ring detectors) carry positive corner weights. Unit 2 is strongly benign: summing through layers 2 and 3 gives about -21,000 integer units. Unit 9 is strongly malignant at about +40,000. A bright top-right corner therefore suppresses the benign pathway and excites the malignant pathway, raising the logit.
answer.evidence: Corner weights, rows 0-2, cols 22-23: unit 27: -33 -30 / -44 -20 / -35 -44. Unit 2: -21 -21 / -14 -33 / -24 -22 (row 3 also -26 -23). Unit 15: r1 c23 -37, r2 -33 -21. Unit 20: r1 c23 -33, r2 c22 -32. Unit 28: r0 -22 -26, r1 c23 -26. Unit 31: r1-r3 c23 -22 -32 -24. Unit 13: r1 -23 -24, r2 c22 -23. Unit 3: r1 c22 -28, r2-r3 c23 -23 -22. In contrast, unit 9 has r0-r3 cols 22-23 = 28 14 / 23 13 / 22 4 / 18 26. Unit 6 has r0 c23 30, r2 c23 27, r3 c22 20. Unit 30 has r0 c23 21, r1 c23 19, r2 c22 16. Neighbouring top-row pixels outside this corner carry small, inconsistent weights in these units. A peripheral 30-mm-crop corner should carry no nodule information, so the sign-consistent pattern across opposing pathways marks a learned spurious cue.
answer.main_feature: Nodule size/extent via centre-surround filters. Units with a small bright core and a dark surrounding ring (e.g. 2, 8, 13, 20) signal a small well-circumscribed nodule and push benign. Units with a dark core and a bright ring or lower field (e.g. 6, 9, 10, 12, 16, 30, 19, 23) respond to larger nodules extending beyond the centre and push malignant.
